missions.title: Clue Market
missions.topic: Irregular plurals · there is / are · how many
missions.subtitle: Count the village supplies
missions.guide: Tap the correct word block. Help the market count its supplies!
missions.reminder: Children and mice are irregular plurals. Match is or are to the number of things. Use how many for things we count.

tasks.prompt: Two ___ are playing outside. One is a boy and one is a girl.
tasks.full: Two children are playing outside.
tasks.hint: Child has the irregular plural children.
tasks.explain: Use children after two, not child or childs.

tasks.prompt: Three ___ are near the cheese. Each one is a little mouse.
tasks.full: Three mice are near the cheese.
tasks.hint: The plural of mouse is mice.
tasks.explain: Mice is the irregular plural form used after three.

tasks.prompt: One bag is on the chair. There ___ one bag on the chair.
tasks.full: There is one bag on the chair.
tasks.hint: One bag is singular.
tasks.explain: There is agrees with the singular noun bag.

tasks.prompt: I put one box on the stall. My friend adds two boxes. There ___ three boxes now.
tasks.full: There are three boxes on the stall now.
tasks.hint: One box and two boxes make more than one box.
tasks.explain: Three boxes is plural, so the sentence uses are.

tasks.prompt: There are six children in the shop. How ___ children are there?
tasks.full: How many children are there?
tasks.hint: Children are people we can count.
tasks.explain: How many asks for the number of countable things or people.

missions.title: Ownership Bridge
missions.topic: her · our · us · them · ownership clues
missions.subtitle: Help your friends cross
missions.guide: Tap the correct pronoun block. Build a bridge for your friends!
missions.reminder: Find who owns the item or who receives the action. Her and our come before nouns; us and them replace people after an action or preposition.

tasks.prompt: A girl called Mila owns the green bag. This is ___ bag.
tasks.full: This is her bag.
tasks.hint: Use her before a noun belonging to the girl.
tasks.explain: Her shows that the bag belongs to Mila.

tasks.prompt: Adam and I share this room. This is ___ room.
tasks.full: This is our room.
tasks.hint: Adam and I means we.
tasks.explain: Our shows that the room belongs to both of us.

tasks.prompt: Mum is calling Adam and me. She is calling ___.
tasks.full: She is calling us.
tasks.hint: Adam and me includes the speaker. Use the object form us.
tasks.explain: Us replaces Adam and me after calling.

tasks.prompt: These books belong to Lina and Mei. Please give the books to ___.
tasks.full: Please give the books to them.
tasks.hint: Lina and Mei are two people. An object pronoun is needed after to.
tasks.explain: Them replaces the two owners after the preposition to.

tasks.prompt: A boy has a blue cap and his sister has a red cap. The red cap is ___ cap.
tasks.full: The red cap is her cap.
tasks.hint: Find the owner of the red cap, not the blue one.
tasks.explain: The sister owns the red cap, so her is the correct possessive adjective.

missions.title: Routine Train
missions.topic: always · sometimes · never · often · how often
missions.subtitle: Build a daily routine
missions.guide: Tap the word carriages in order. Build a routine to move the train!
missions.reminder: Always, sometimes, never and often usually come before the main verb. After do or does in these questions, use the base verb.

tasks.prompt: Describe her routine. Start with She; put always before walks.
tasks.full: She always walks to school.
tasks.hint: Use She always walks, then to school.
tasks.explain: Always goes before walks; use walks after She.

tasks.prompt: Describe a routine. Start with We; put sometimes before play.
tasks.answer: We sometimes play football after school.
tasks.full: We sometimes play football after school.
tasks.hint: Use We sometimes play, then football after school.
tasks.explain: Sometimes tells us how often we play football.

tasks.prompt: Describe his routine. Start with He; put never before eats.
tasks.full: He never eats meat.
tasks.hint: Use He never eats, then meat.
tasks.explain: Never means at no time. Use eats with He.

tasks.prompt: Ask a routine question. Start with Do; put often before read.
tasks.answer: Do you often read at night?
tasks.full: Do you often read at night?
tasks.hint: Use Do you often read, then at night.
tasks.explain: A present simple question uses Do you and the base verb read.

tasks.prompt: Ask about her tennis routine. Start with How often.
tasks.answer: How often does she play tennis?
tasks.full: How often does she play tennis?
tasks.hint: Use How often does she, then the base verb play.
tasks.explain: Does she is followed by play, not plays. How often asks about frequency.

missions.title: Action River
missions.subtitle: Build actions happening now
missions.guide: Put the word blocks in order. Build a boat with an action happening now!
missions.reminder: Use am, is or are with an ing verb. Put not after the helping verb. In a question, the helping verb comes before the subject.

tasks.prompt: Describe what is happening now. Start with The.
tasks.full: The boys are swimming.
tasks.hint: The boys is plural. Use are before swimming.
tasks.explain: Are swimming describes what the boys are doing now.

tasks.prompt: Describe the girl now. Start with My.
tasks.answer: My sister is drawing a cat.
tasks.full: My sister is drawing a cat.
tasks.hint: Use My sister is, then drawing a cat.
tasks.explain: My sister is one person, so use is drawing.

tasks.prompt: Say that they are not playing now. Start with They; finish with now.
tasks.answer: They are not playing football now.
tasks.full: They are not playing football now.
tasks.hint: Put not between are and playing.
tasks.explain: The negative present continuous uses are not plus an ing verb.

tasks.prompt: Ask about your brother now. Start with Is.
tasks.answer: Is your brother reading a book?
tasks.full: Is your brother reading a book?
tasks.hint: Use Is your brother, then reading a book.
tasks.explain: Move is before the subject to form a present continuous question.

tasks.prompt: Ask about the children now. Start with What; finish with now.
tasks.answer: What are the children doing now?
tasks.full: What are the children doing now?
tasks.hint: Use What are the children, then doing now.
tasks.explain: Use are with children; What asks about the action.

missions.title: Story Mine
missions.topic: Past stories · went · found · were · broke · put
missions.subtitle: Find words from the past
missions.guide: Tap the correct word block. Find a gem for each action from yesterday!
missions.reminder: Keep completed story events in the past. Some past forms change, such as go to went. Put stays put in the past.

tasks.prompt: Yesterday, our class ___ to the zoo by bus.
tasks.full: Yesterday, our class went to the zoo by bus.
tasks.hint: Yesterday needs the past form of go.
tasks.explain: Went is the irregular past form of go.

tasks.prompt: Yesterday, Aina ___ a small shell on the beach.
tasks.full: Yesterday, Aina found a small shell on the beach.
tasks.hint: Find changes to found in the past.
tasks.explain: Found describes the completed action yesterday.

tasks.prompt: The children ___ at school yesterday, but today they are at home.
tasks.full: The children were at school yesterday.
tasks.hint: Children is plural, and yesterday is in the past.
tasks.explain: Use were for a plural subject in the past.

tasks.prompt: Ben dropped his glass. It ___ on the floor.
tasks.full: It broke on the floor.
tasks.hint: Dropped begins a past event. Continue with a past verb.
tasks.explain: Broke continues the story in the past; breaks is present and breaking needs a helping verb.

tasks.prompt: Ben drank some water. Then he ___ the empty cup on the table.
tasks.full: Then he put the empty cup on the table.
tasks.hint: Drank and then show a sequence of completed past actions.
tasks.explain: The past form of put stays put. He puts would describe a present routine.

missions.title: Choice Portal
missions.topic: and · or · but · match meaning to clues
missions.subtitle: Join the story blocks
missions.guide: Read the story clue. Tap a linking word to open the portal!
missions.reminder: And adds. Or gives a choice. But joins different or opposite ideas.

tasks.prompt: Would you like milk ___ juice? Please choose one drink.
tasks.full: Would you like milk or juice?
tasks.hint: Or gives a choice between two things.
tasks.explain: The speaker asks the listener to choose one drink, so use or.

tasks.prompt: Mia has a ruler ___ a pencil. She has both things.
tasks.full: Mia has a ruler and a pencil.
tasks.hint: Both things are included.
tasks.explain: And adds one item to another.

tasks.prompt: Ben has a new bike, ___ he cannot ride it yet.
tasks.full: Ben has a new bike, but he cannot ride it yet.
tasks.hint: Having a bike and being unable to ride it are contrasting ideas.
tasks.explain: But joins the unexpected contrast between owning a bike and being unable to ride it.

tasks.prompt: There is one snack for you. Take an apple ___ a banana; do not take both.
tasks.full: Take an apple or a banana.
tasks.hint: The instruction allows only one of the two snacks.
tasks.explain: Or matches a choice of one snack rather than both.

tasks.prompt: The bag looks small, ___ it can hold many books.
tasks.full: The bag looks small, but it can hold many books.
tasks.hint: Holding many books is unexpected for a small-looking bag.
tasks.explain: But connects the contrast between the appearance and what the bag can hold.

missions.title: Hideout Rescue
missions.subtitle: Give the cat a safe place
missions.guide: Tap the cat, then tap its place. You can also drag the cat!
missions.reminder: Read the place word. In is inside. Behind is at the back. Between is in the middle.

tasks.prompt: Put the cat in the box, not on the table.
tasks.full: The cat is in the box.
tasks.hint: Choose the inside of the box.
tasks.explain: In describes a position inside the box.

tasks.prompt: The cat is below the table top. Put it under the table.
tasks.full: The cat is under the table.
tasks.hint: Choose the space beneath the table.
tasks.explain: Under means below the table, not on top of it.

tasks.prompt: Keep the cat off the floor. Put it on the table top.
tasks.full: The cat is on the table.
tasks.hint: Choose the top surface of the table.
tasks.explain: On describes the cat resting on the table top.

tasks.prompt: The cat is outdoors. It is not at the table or in the box. Hide it behind the tree.
tasks.full: The cat is behind the tree.
tasks.hint: Choose the hiding place at the back of the tree.
tasks.explain: Behind places the cat at the back of the tree rather than at the table or in the box.

tasks.prompt: The cat needs a place outside the box and away from the table. Put it between the two rocks.
tasks.full: The cat is between the rocks.
tasks.hint: Find the middle space with a rock on each side.
tasks.explain: Between describes the middle position with one rock on each side.

missions.title: Clue Castle
missions.subtitle: Compare two objects
missions.guide: Look at both objects. Tap the one that matches the words!
missions.reminder: Taller and shorter compare heights. Bigger and smaller compare sizes.

tasks.prompt: Tap the tower that is taller than the other tower.
tasks.full: Tower B is taller than Tower A.
tasks.hint: Compare the heights. Choose the tower that reaches higher.
tasks.explain: Taller compares the heights of the two towers.

tasks.prompt: Choose the tower that is smaller than the other tower.
tasks.full: Tower B is smaller than Tower A.
tasks.hint: Compare the overall sizes of the two towers.
tasks.explain: Smaller compares the sizes of two objects.

tasks.prompt: Tap the tower that is taller than Tower A but shorter than Tower C.
tasks.full: Tower B is taller than Tower A but shorter than Tower C.
tasks.hint: Find one tower that fits both comparisons.
tasks.explain: Tower B is above A in height and below C, so both parts are true.

tasks.prompt: Choose a tower that is shorter than Tower A but taller than Tower B.
tasks.full: Tower C is shorter than Tower A but taller than Tower B.
tasks.hint: Do not choose A or B. Compare the remaining tower with each one.
tasks.explain: Tower C fits both comparisons: it is lower than A and higher than B.

tasks.prompt: The tower you need is bigger than Tower C and smaller than Tower B. Which tower fits both clues?
tasks.full: Tower A is bigger than Tower C and smaller than Tower B.
tasks.hint: Check both size clues before choosing.
tasks.explain: Tower A is larger than C and smaller than B; the other towers fail one of the clues.

rules: shop
Count the clues
one child → two children · one mouse → three mice
Use there is with one thing and there are with more than one. Ask how many for a number.
There are three boxes. How many children are there?
bridge
Owners and objects
her bag · our room · calling us · give to them
Find the owner first. Use an object pronoun after an action or a preposition.
Mum is calling Adam and me. She is calling us.
train
How often?
always · sometimes · never · often
These frequency words go before the main verb in our sentences. Use a base verb after do or does.
She always walks to school. How often does she play tennis?
boat
Actions now
They are swimming. · They are not playing. · Is he reading?
Use am, is or are with an ing verb. Change the word order to ask a question.
What are the children doing now?
pickaxe
Past story clues
go → went · find → found · break → broke · put → put
Yesterday, completed events and then can show a past story. Keep the verb in the past.
Ben drank some water. Then he put the cup on the table.
portal
Choose the link
and = both · or = choose · but = contrast
Read both ideas before choosing the joining word.
The bag looks small, but it can hold many books.
cat
Find the place
in · on · under · behind · between
Read all the position clues, then choose the matching place.
The cat is between the two rocks.
castle
Use both clues
taller than A · shorter than C
One tower must fit both comparisons. Check the first clue and then the second.
Tower B is taller than Tower A but shorter than Tower C.

curriculum.title: DSKP Bahasa Inggeris SK Tahun 3 — Primary Year 3 English Language Syllabus
curriculum.grammarPages: Printed pages 43–45 (PDF pages 57–59); recycled Year 1–2 structures in Appendix 2
learningStandards: 3.2.2: Read details in short, simple texts.
4.2.4: Describe people and objects with suitable vocabulary.
4.2.5: Link sentences with basic coordinating conjunctions.
4.3.1: Practise capitals and sentence punctuation through guided word ordering.
4.3.3: Plan and form a range of simple sentences.
curriculum.note: Original 3K practice: exactly 20 medium and 20 upper-medium activities within Year 3 SK language. Medium items apply a grammar pattern to a short familiar context. Upper-medium items add connected clues, pronoun reference, question word order, contrast or two comparisons; they do not introduce a higher-year grammar syllabus. Selected Year 3 grammar: irregular plurals, subject/object/possessive pronouns, frequency adverbs, conjunctions, past simple, prepositions and short-adjective comparisons. Present simple and continuous recycle Year 2 language as permitted. Difficulty labels are design categories, not PBD or CEFR levels.
